systemDesign.title: System Design Interview
systemDesign.description: 10 classic system design problems with architecture walkthroughs

whatIs.title: What is System Design Interview?
whatIs.description: A technical interview format that evaluates your ability to design large-scale systems. You'll design architectures for real services like URL shorteners, chat systems, and news feeds, covering requirements analysis, estimation, component design, and scalability.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Click a problem card to view the detailed walkthrough
Use practice mode to rehearse step-by-step answers
Study the 5 tabs in order: Requirements → Estimation → Architecture → Deep Dive → Scalability
Review ASCII diagrams to visualize the overall architecture
Check interview tips for what interviewers expect

tips.title: Interview Tips
items: Clarify requirements first — interviewers value this process
Back-of-envelope estimation is about logical thinking, not exact numbers
When explaining tradeoffs, clearly state WHY you chose one approach over another
If short on time, prioritize breadth over depth, but go deep when the interviewer probes

items.q: Should juniors prepare for system design?
items.a: Basic design sense helps even juniors. Start with intermediate level (URL Shortener, Rate Limiter, Notification System).

items.q: How do you draw diagrams in real interviews?
items.a: Use a whiteboard or online tools like Excalidraw. Focus on key components and data flow.

items.q: How to allocate time in a 45-min interview?
items.a: Requirements 5min, Estimation 5min, High-level Design 15min, Deep Dive 15min, Q&A 5min.
